title: Yedidim: Israeli volunteers who help stranded drivers and people in distress for free

trailer.text: Yedidim is a nationwide volunteer organization in Israel, and its Israeli volunteers give a helping hand to those in need.
The volunteers help drivers in need and in emergencies at no cost, and also rescue people from elevators and help the elderly with urgent home repairs.
According to ISRAEL21c, Israel Almasi came up with the idea for Yedidim when his car got stuck one rainy winter day and no one stopped to help him, and today he is the CEO of the nonprofit.
No one in the organization, up to the CEO, receives a salary.

stations.title: A car stuck on a rainy day

paragraphs.text: According to ISRAEL21c, Israel Almasi came up with the idea for Yedidim when his car got stuck one rainy winter day and no one stopped to help him.
He said he waited an hour and a half for someone to stop and help him.
According to Arutz 7, the incident stayed with him, and he decided that what had happened to him would not happen to others.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Almasi set up a WhatsApp group so that people who got stuck could reach someone.
According to ISRAEL21c, he discovered that many people are willing to help.
According to ESRA Magazine, Rabbi Meir Weiner established the organization in 2006, inspired by a friends' organization in the US.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Weiner and volunteers sought to assist drivers on Highway 443, at whom stones were thrown almost every day.
According to Arutz 7, when calls came in from Route 443, they tried to hurry and help.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Almasi heard about Yedidim and approached Winer, who told him he could take charge of the group.
According to Arutz 7, Weiner's group faded when WhatsApp was born, and Almasi revived it.
Yedidim help drivers in need and in emergencies at no cost.
According to Maariv, they assist with starting vehicles, filling fluids and opening locked vehicles without damage.
The volunteers also rescue people from elevators, help the elderly and the needy with urgent home repairs, deliver emergency supplies and extract vehicles.
According to Maariv, the nonprofit gives non-medical first aid on the roads and in homes, 24 hours a day.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the volunteers operate 24 hours a day, six days a week.
Yedidim does not operate on Shabbat and holidays, nor in Palestinian Authority territories.

stations.title: From the call to the changed tire

paragraphs.text: Volunteer operators answer calls in Hebrew, English, Arabic and Russian.
The call is forwarded to local teams of volunteers, connected through WhatsApp groups or a dedicated app.
According to Maariv, the yellow chain added to its app a Yedidim rescue button, which opens a call at the call center.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the dispatchers receive an average of 18,000 calls a week, and the volunteers respond to approximately 6,000 calls a week from people in distress.
According to ISRAEL21c, 2,000 to 3,000 callers ask for help every day, from all sectors.
Almasi said the organization aims to reach every call within 13 minutes at most.
According to the Jerusalem Post, Yedidim hopes to cut the average response time from 28:40 minutes to about 13 minutes.
In a Ynetnews article, three motorcycles arrived within 15 minutes of the call, and changed a tire in less than five minutes.
According to ISRAEL21c, a volunteer arrived within 20 minutes with a portable charger and revived Yoel's car.
Almasi said the organization has 16 motorcycles that were donated, and that the goal is 5,000.

stations.title: The volunteers: training, equipment, money out of pocket

paragraphs.text: According to ISRAEL21c, the volunteers are aged 16 to 89, and they undergo a training course on car maintenance.
Every volunteer undergoes three hours of basic training, which includes changing tires.
No one in the organization, up to the CEO, receives a salary.
Almasi himself works as a project manager at a credit-card company.
The volunteers must buy their own equipment.
According to Bishansky, the average volunteer spends NIS 800 to 1,000 of their own money on equipment.
Yedidim negotiates with suppliers so that the volunteers can buy equipment at a discount.
According to Maariv, yellow donated more than 1,000 rescue kits for volunteers to the nonprofit.
The Bird company will allow volunteers to ride scooters for free, with a special coupon code in the app.
According to Arutz 7, until recently the organization did not agree to accept donations.
According to Arutz 7, the volunteers are divided into districts and regions.
Each source reports a different number of volunteers: Channel 7 reports 6,500, Ynetnews more than 56 thousand, and ISRAEL21c in 2024 reports 65 thousand.
Almasi said that on average five to eight children a day are rescued from locked cars.
The sources give different numbers of children rescued, in different years.
In May 2021, during the missile fire, Yedidim helped people operate windows and doors of safe rooms, about 6,000 of them.
According to Almasi, in 2020 there were more than 400,000 Covid-related events, including the transport of tens of thousands of food baskets and medicines.
Select volunteers trained with the army and the Home Front Command, to assist in a building collapse or a national emergency.
According to ice, on the instruction of rabbis, the Yedidim call center was opened on Shabbat and the Simchat Torah holiday.
According to ice, volunteers worked many hours, day and night, evacuating the dead, while preserving their dignity.
Yedidim helped transport reservist soldiers to bases, and move equipment and food to the fighters and to the residents of the south.
According to ISRAEL21c, after October 7 Almasi saw hundreds of cars parked near army bases.
Almasi explained that two volunteers need to be sent, so that one drives the car and the other returns.
The car-return project helped return thousands of cars to the families of reservist soldiers.
A summary line on the ISRAEL21c website states that 60 thousand Yedidim volunteers answer calls related to the war and to practical aid throughout Israel.

stations.title: An award, and people from all sectors

paragraphs.text: Yedidim won the President's Award.
According to ISRAEL21c, the organization received the President's Award for Volunteerism.
According to the Jerusalem Post, a Muslim volunteer came to help a religious family from Bnei Brak.
Almasi said that Arabs, Christians, Jews, religious and secular people unite in helping each other.
According to Channel 7, the volunteer base started in the Haredi sector, but today everyone is in it, even a few women.
According to Almasi, at-risk youth and people with disabilities are integrated into the call center and the volunteer network.
Startach developed for Yedidim a service for the hard of hearing and the deaf, who could not use the service.
According to Arutz 7, the organization gives priority to women, and will always come to give them fuel, cables or help changing a tire.
Almasi said the goal is half a million volunteers, a volunteer in every building.
According to a blog on the Times of Israel, after 45 minutes of waiting for Yedidim they called a friend for advice.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the average response time stood at 28:40 minutes.

According to Channel 7, a Yedidim volunteer who came to refuel a car stuck on a highway waited more than 20 minutes for the traffic police patrol car he had called to the scene, and no patrol car arrived.
According to Arutz 7, the volunteers give with all their heart, but are not willing to be exploited.
Soria said that volunteers detect exploitation, and use the opportunity to teach the callers again.

claims.quote: הסעת חיילי מילואים לבסיסים ולאזורי כינוס, שינוע ציוד ואוכל ללוחמים ולתושבי הדרום

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c, אלמסי ראה מאות רכבים חונים ליד בסיסי צבא אחרי 7 באוקטובר.
claims.quote: after seeing hundreds of cars parked on the side of the road outside army bases post October 7

claims.text: אלמסי הסביר שיש לשלוח שני מתנדבים, כדי שאחד יוביל את הרכב והשני יחזור.
claims.quote: two volunteers have to be dispatched so that one can drive the car to its destination and be transported back

claims.text: פרויקט החזרת הרכבים סייע להחזיר אלפי רכבים למשפחות חיילי המילואים.
claims.quote: which has helped get thousands of cars returned to the families of reservist soldiers

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c, 60 אלף מתנדבי ידידים ענו לקריאות הקשורות למלחמה ולסיוע מעשי ברחבי ישראל.
claims.quote: 60,000 Yedidim volunteers answer war-related calls for practical aid throughout Israel.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, מתנדב מוסלמי הגיע לעזור למשפחה דתית מבני ברק.
claims.quote: Recently, a Muslim volunteer came to assist a religious family from Bnei Brak.

claims.text: אלמסי אמר שערבים, נוצרים, יהודים, דתיים וחילונים מתאחדים בעזרה הדדית.
claims.quote: Arabs, Christians, Jews, religious or secular, we succeed in a time of the worst catastrophe to close the gaps and unite people in helping each other

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, בסיס המתנדבים החל מהמגזר החרדי אך כיום כולם משתתפים, גם נשים.
claims.quote: בסיס המתנדבים החל מהמגזר החרדי, אבל היום כולם נמצאים בו, אפילו כמה נשים

claims.text: לפי אלמסי, נוער בסיכון ובעלי מוגבלויות משולבים במוקד וברשת המתנדבים.
claims.quote: Almasi says that at-risk youth and people with physical disabilities are integrated

claims.text: סטארטאח פיתחו עבור ידידים שירות לכבדי שמיעה וחירשים שלא יכלו להשתמש בשירות.
claims.quote: שכבדי שמיעה וחירשים אינם יכולים להשתמש בשירות שהם מציעים

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, לנשים הארגון נותן עדיפות ותמיד יגיע לתת דלק, כבלים או עזרה בהחלפת גלגל.
claims.quote: תמיד יגיעו לתת להן דלק, כבלים או סיוע בהחלפת גלגל

claims.text: אלמסי אמר שהמטרה היא חצי מיליון מתנדבים, מתנדב בכל בניין.
claims.quote: My goal is to have half a million volunteers, a volunteer in each building

claims.text: לפי בלוג בטיימס אוף ישראל, אחרי 45 דקות של המתנה לידידים התקשרו לחבר לעצה.
claims.quote: But after 45 minutes, we called a friend in the neighborhood for advice.

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, מתנדב המתין 20 דקות ואף ניידת משטרה לא הגיעה.
claims.quote: 20 דקות חלפו, אפילו קצת יותר, אבל אף ניידת לא הגיעה

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, המתנדבים נותנים מכל הלב אך לא מוכנים להיות מנוצלים.
claims.quote: החברים כאן נותנים מכל הלב, אבל לא מוכנים להיות מנוצלים

claims.text: סוריה אמר שמתנדבים מזהים ניצול ומנצלים את ההזדמנות ללמד שוב את הפונים.
claims.quote: But we know how to detect that and use the opportunity to teach them again

claims.text: אלמסי אמר לג'רוזלם פוסט שחיכה שעה וחצי בגשם לרכב אחר.
claims.quote: an hour and a half in the rain for another car to come

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, אלמסי חיכה שעתיים, רטוב וקפוא, עד שהגיע המושיע.
claims.quote: רק אחרי שעתיים, כשהוא רטוב, קופא מקור ומתוסכל, הגיע המושיע.

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), וינר הקים את ידידים בזמן האינתיפאדה השנייה כדי לעזור למי שנתקע ביהודה ושומרון.
claims.quote: Founded by Meir Winer during the Second Intifada in order to help people whose cars got stuck in the West Bank

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2018), ידידים הם קבוצה של 8,500 מתנדבים ברחבי הארץ.
claims.quote: He was part of Yedidim, a group of 8,500 volunteers around the country who are only a phone call away

claims.text: לפי מגזין ESRA, יש 18,073 מתנדבים ברחבי הארץ, גברים ונשים.
claims.quote: There are 18,073 volunteers across the country, both men and women

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט (2020), יש 20 אלף מתנדבי ידידים ברחבי הארץ.
claims.quote: Hermon to Eilat, there are 20,000 Yedidim (“Friends”) volunteers at the ready

claims.text: לפי ג'רוזלם פוסט, בידידים יש יותר מ-36 אלף מתנדבים.
claims.quote: and has more than 36,000 volunteers. It provides assistance 24/7 to help people stuck on roads and in buildings

claims.text: לפי ISRAEL21c (2021), ידידים גייס כ-36 אלף מתנדבים בכל הארץ, מוכנים לכל מקרה חירום לא רפואי.
claims.quote: Yedidim has recruited some 36,000 volunteers up and down the country, ready to aid in any non-medical emergency, big or small.

sources.label: Times of Israel, blog, Alan Silverstein
